proof_review: Normality makes G-membership constant on each Q-conjugacy class. Class representatives filtered by order two and membership in G exhaust the involutions in G intersect Q.
For x^a=a^-1*x*a, y^d and y^dprime lie in the same S-orbit exactly when dprime lies in C_Q(y)*d*S. Left/right orientation is correct.
S fixes H pointwise, so removing representatives in H discards exactly the forbidden orbits.
NormalClosure(Q, <class representatives>) generates all involutions of the pool and stays in G. The full normal closure, rather than only representatives, is implemented.
For a child, Q equals the old S and the new S is Centralizer(old S,x). Sharing nextPool across siblings preserves these invariants.

The inherited intersection recursion is called only on independent extensions of accepted prefixes, so its hypothesis holds. The subgroup-index depth bound, generation and reversal tests remain valid.
limitations: A semantic review and Test/E6 control comparison, not source admission or completed large census.
Identification of PrimitiveGroup(276,3) with Co3 is not part of this review.
GAP exact group, conjugacy, normal closure, centralizer and double-coset algorithms are software premises. The sum of double-coset sizes is only a consistency check.
